messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 PagerDuty: High embeddings queue latency detected in eu-west-1. Alert: embeddings-queue-latency > 2s for 5m. Trigger: autoscaler not adding pods. Incident ID: INC-2026-3247

pagerbot: :rotating_light: PD page fired to #incidents and on-call. Escalation policy: embeddings-slo. Initial severity: P2.

morgan: oncall here, grabbing this. checking if it's an autoscaler or k8s issue.

anya: thanks — can you post the recent grafana spike link? customer CS pinged about slow embeddings in prod (eu).

morgan: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/embeds/queue?orgId=1&from=now-30m to=now — 99th jumped to ~4.8s around 00:12 UTC.

incident-bot: note: runbook step 1 -> check pods: `kubectl -n inference get hpa,deploy,svc`

morgan: running checks now.

morgan: `kubectl -n inference get hpa embeddings-workers` -> TARGET CPU 60% current 95% replicas stuck at 3/5. HPA not scaling, API errors 429 from metrics-server.

tj: I can try to manually scale replicas while we figure out HPA. `kubectl scale deploy embeddings-workers --replicas=8 -n inference`

morgan: please do, tj. doing a quick sanity of node capacity.

devon: tagging in infra — could be autoscaler permissions or metrics server flapping. I'll look at cluster events.

pj? (sidenote) pagerbot: :white_check_mark: morgan acknowledged the page.

tj: scaled to 8. New pods scheduled. watch logs for warmup KV cache pressure.

anya: customer-success — what's the customer impact? any outgoing tickets?

customer-success: We have one enterprise customer (AcmeCorp) reporting slow ingestion and 5-10 min embedding delays for some pipelines. Escalated to CS manager, they want ETA and mitigation steps.

morgan: seeing latency drop at the queue level after scale — p99 down to ~2.1s in the last 2m. Still higher than normal but improving.

devon: cluster events show `metrics-server` OOMKilled repeatedly around the alert time; HPA couldn't read metrics. Restarted the metrics-server DaemonSet. I'm opening a bug: https://issues.redwood.example/INFR-612

morgan: good call. Can we add a fallback to not rely solely on metrics-server for HPA decisions? (runbook improvement)

anya: noted — will file a runbook PR after the incident. For now CS asked for a short message to customers: "We're mitigating an embeddings latency issue in EU, scaling workers and monitoring. No data loss. Expect improved latency in ~5-10m." Anyone object?

tj: fine by me. I'd add that it's due to autoscaling telemetry interruption.

customer-success: sending message now. tagging legal for FYI.

pagerbot: :information_source: Escalation update: severity remains P2. No SLA breach yet. Next check-in in 10m.

morgan: current ask — can ops-sre rotate metrics-server to a larger instance type or bump memory? It keeps restarting and HPA will flake otherwise.

devon: doing a hotpatch bump to metrics-server resources to 512Mi -> apply now.

incident-bot: action logged: metrics-server memory increased. `kubectl apply -f metrics-server-hotpatch.yaml` by devon at 1719010200.

morgan: p99 now ~1.3s and falling. Embedding ingestion backlog draining. Looks stable.

anya: customer-success confirmed customer saw improvement. We're preparing a post-incident note for the CS thread.

tj: recommend followups: (1) add HPA fallback to CPU average if metrics-server unavailable, (2) alert for metrics-server restarts, (3) investigate why it OOMed.

devon: logged infra bug with heap dump request and a tentative remediation plan.

morgan: handing off to the morning oncall for follow-up and RCA. @anya, can you own the customer postmortem and share with AcmeCorp?

anya: yep will draft and loop in CS manager.

pagerbot: :white_check_mark: incident INC-2026-3247 marked as mitigated. Owner: morgan -> handing to morning-oncall for RCA.

morgan: thanks everyone. final note: no data lost, short-term fix applied, follow-ups assigned. Closing thread in 30m unless regression. :tada:
